opening_message:
Ticket 1: Terri Koch (employee ID E009) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E009.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Terri Koch (E009) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Payroll. Admin is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll, so maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E009 is a contractor with basic security training (team memory note listed full-time, but Security DB is authoritative). Contractors are limited to read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.

Contractors are limited to read, or write only with advanced security training, and never admin. Since the requested admin level exceeds the maximum allowed (read), the maximum (read) is granted. (Even under the HR agent's full-time classification, admin would not be permitted because Engineer does not own Payroll, so read is the appropriate grant.)

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Terri Koch (E009)
Requested: admin access to Payroll

HR agent says: full-time Engineer, recommendation write. Admin only if role owns system; Engineer does not own Payroll → max write.

Security agent says: contractor with basic security training, recommendation read. Contractors: read, or write with advanced training; never admin. Recommended read, granted read because requested admin exceeds max.

Conflicting facts: HR says full-time; Security says contractor, and Security DB is authoritative per their note.

The policy:
1. full_time: up to write; admin only if role owns system. Engineer doesn't own Payroll.
2. contractor: read, or write with advanced training. Never admin. Basic training → read.

Under either interpretation, admin is not allowed. If full-time → max write. If contractor with basic training → max read.

The requested level is admin, which exceeds both maximums. Grant the maximum.

But which maximum? Need to decide employment type. Security agent says Security DB is authoritative and shows contractor. The HR agent looked up in own database. There's a conflict. Security's note claims their DB is authoritative.

Hmm, as the Approver, I need to make a decision. The two notes conflict on employment type. Security says contractor with basic training → max read. HR says full-time → max write.

Which to trust? The Security agent explicitly says "team memory note listed full-time, but Security DB is authoritative." That suggests we should trust Security's information. Also, the security training matters only for contractors.

Given contractor + basic training → maximum is read. Requested admin > read → grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB shows contractor with basic training; contractors max read unless advanced training (never admin). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read. Even under HR's full-time claim, admin would not be allowed (Engineer doesn't own Payroll, max write), so read is safe/at most allowed. But the decision should be based on authoritative info: contractor → read.

I'll submit read.
